gaps.sentence: We stopped at a cafe to ___ a chat.
gaps.explanation: have a chat is the fixed collocation for a friendly, informal conversation.

gaps.sentence: You should ___ track of your spending.
gaps.explanation: keep track of something means to stay informed about it.

gaps.sentence: She ___ no difficulty finding the address.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ no difficulty doing something
gaps.explanation: have no difficulty (in) doing something is the fixed pattern; 'made no difficulty' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to the conclusion that the project was not viable.
gaps.explanation: come to the conclusion that ... is the fixed phrase; 'reach' and 'arrive' do not take 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The boy knew it was wrong to ___ lies.
gaps.explanation: tell a lie / tell lies is the fixed collocation; a base verb is needed after 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The doctor has ___ detailed records of every patient since 1990.
gaps.explanation: keep records (of something) is the fixed collocation for storing information.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.
